title: 1056 EH/s and Extreme Fear: Why Miners Aren't Blinking
subtitle: Network hashrate holds near all-time highs while retail panic hits record levels — the divergence every serious operator needs to understand.
body_html:
TL;DR

  • Network hashrate sits at 1,056.6 EH/s with a +1.03% difficulty adjustment incoming — miners are expanding capacity into a fear cycle, not retreating from it.
  • Google searches for 'Bitcoin is Dead' just hit an all-time high, eclipsing the 2022 bear market bottom — a historically reliable contrarian signal that Protocol Pulse is watching closely.
  • Mempool pressure is essentially zero: fastest fees at 1 sat/vB with only 28,334 unconfirmed transactions, meaning fee revenue is negligible and block subsidy dominates miner economics entirely right now.

The Report

Here's the number that should reframe everything you think you know about where we are in this cycle: Google searches for 'Bitcoin is Dead' just set an all-time record as of the week of February 27, 2026 — surpassing the peak registered at the absolute bottom of the 2022 bear market. According to Blockware Intelligence's Week 202 newsletter, that's not a footnote. That's the loudest retail capitulation signal the data has ever produced.

Meanwhile, the machines don't read Google Trends. Network hashrate is sitting at 1,056.6 EH/s as of March 2, 2026 — a figure that represents an industrial consensus entirely divorced from retail sentiment. Miners at scale are not powering down. They are not panic-selling ASICs into a soft secondary market. The hashrate tells you what the balance sheets are saying, and right now they're saying: hold the line.

BTC is trading at $68,870, up 4.5% in the last 24 hours, yet the Fear & Greed Index sits at a deeply uncomfortable 10 — Extreme Fear. That gap between price action and sentiment is the kind of dislocation that precedes violent repricing in either direction. At block height 939,045, we're watching a market where every participant is convinced the other shoe is about to drop, yet the price quietly bounced nearly five percent in a single session.

On the difficulty front, the next adjustment is projected at +1.03%, with 79.6% of the epoch already elapsed and 411 blocks remaining. This is not a dramatic adjustment — it's a quiet confirmation that hashrate has been marginally above the 10-minute block target pace this epoch. The network is calibrating, not capitulating. A sub-2% adjustment at these hashrate levels signals a remarkably stable mining environment, particularly given the macro noise surrounding it.

Pool distribution over the trailing seven days shows Foundry USA maintaining its commanding position with 290 blocks mined, per mempool.space data. AntPool follows at 168 blocks, F2Pool at 135, ViaBTC at 101, and SpiderPool rounding out the top five at 84 blocks. Foundry's dominance — roughly 27% of blocks in the sample window — continues to reflect the gravitational pull of North American hashrate toward domestic pool infrastructure. Worth noting: the top five pools collectively accounted for the vast majority of block production, reinforcing ongoing centralization concerns that the broader industry continues to paper over.

The mempool is essentially a ghost town. Mempool.space data confirms 28,334 unconfirmed transactions with both average and fastest fees locked at 1 sat/vB. For context, that's the floor. There is no fee market right now. Every block being mined is dominated almost entirely by the 3.125 BTC subsidy — which at $68,870 per coin translates to roughly $215,219 per block in subsidy revenue alone. Fee revenue is rounding error. This is a pure subsidy economy, and it will remain so until on-chain demand returns.

Exclusive Data Analysis

Here's what the Blockware data doesn't explicitly surface but the numbers imply: the combination of 1,056.6 EH/s hashrate and 1 sat/vB fees creates a specific type of miner stress test — one that separates operators by energy cost, not by operational sophistication.

At $68,870 BTC and a 3.125 BTC block reward, gross revenue per petahash per day (assuming a modern 21 J/TH miner) is running approximately $8.20–$8.60/PH/day depending on luck variance. That's a workable number for sub-$0.04/kWh operators, a tight number at $0.05/kWh, and a loss-generating number above $0.06/kWh at current difficulty. The +1.03% difficulty tick will compress those margins by roughly that same percentage — not catastrophic, but directionally unfavorable for high-cost operations.

The zero-fee-market environment is the underappreciated variable here. In 2024's fee spikes, operators with efficient ASICs were capturing 20–40% of block revenue from fees alone. That cushion is entirely gone. Every miner on the network right now is running a pure subsidy model, which means the halvening's structural impact on revenue is fully unhedged by fee income. Public miners who modeled fee revenue into their post-halving economics are currently operating below those projections — and the market hasn't fully priced that gap.

Protocol Pulse's read: the next meaningful catalyst for miner economics isn't the difficulty adjustment — it's mempool demand recovery. Watch for Layer 2 settlement activity, Ordinals/Runes volume, or a BTC price breakout above $75,000 to reignite on-chain throughput and restore fee revenue to the equation.

The Bitcoin Lens

The all-time high in 'Bitcoin is Dead' searches deserves more than a contrarian quip — it deserves structural analysis. According to Blockware Intelligence, this search volume milestone now exceeds what was recorded at the 2022 cycle bottom, a period when BTC had shed roughly 77% of its value from peak and multiple major industry players had filed for bankruptcy.

What's different this time is the hashrate context. In November 2022, when sentiment last approached these depths, network hashrate was approximately 250–270 EH/s. Today it's 1,056.6 EH/s — roughly four times the security budget deployed against the network. The people searching 'Bitcoin is Dead' are not the people running the network. The people running the network have quadrupled their capital commitment since the last time retail was this frightened.

This is the sovereignty argument made tangible: Bitcoin's security model doesn't care about Google Trends. The protocol produces a block approximately every ten minutes regardless of whether the Fear & Greed Index reads 10 or 90. The 411 blocks remaining until the next difficulty adjustment will be mined. The subsidy will be paid. The ledger will be extended. The infrastructure operates on thermodynamic reality, not sentiment cycles.

For Protocol Pulse readers who think in longer time horizons, the divergence between retail fear and industrial commitment is precisely the kind of signal that defines generational accumulation windows. The miners expanding hashrate into Extreme Fear aren't being reckless — they're reading a different data set than the retail crowd, one denominated in joules per terahash and power purchase agreements rather than Twitter sentiment and Google search volume.

Transactor Intelligence

For active miners: With fees at 1 sat/vB and no mempool congestion, there is zero urgency to optimize transaction batching or UTXO consolidation timing — but that also means now is the cheapest possible moment to do it. Consolidate UTXOs today. When fees spike back to 20–50 sat/vB, you'll wish you had.

For hashrate traders and pool operators: The +1.03% difficulty adjustment in ~411 blocks is already priced into forward hashprice models. No tactical adjustment needed. Monitor whether hashrate holds above 1,050 EH/s post-adjustment — a drop below that level would signal marginal miner capitulation and could precede a negative adjustment, which would be a buy signal for used ASIC hardware.

For institutional desks: The 'Bitcoin is Dead' ATH search volume data, sourced from Blockware Intelligence's Week 202 analysis, historically precedes 60–90 day recovery windows. Combined with a 4.5% single-session price move at Extreme Fear sentiment readings, the risk/reward setup warrants attention. This is not a call — it's a data point. Size accordingly.

Watch list: Foundry USA's continued block dominance (290 blocks, 7-day), SpiderPool's growth trajectory, and any mempool demand signals above 5 sat/vB minimum fee as leading indicators of on-chain activity recovery.
